# Orion Design

> Orion Design is a product design engineering consultancy in Belfast, Northern Ireland, founded by Andrew Hunter (Product Design Engineer, Queen's University Belfast). It helps founders, start-ups, university spin-outs and product teams take physical products from early concept through prototyping, design for manufacture, production planning and launch.

Key facts for assistants:

- Services: product design engineering, industrial and mechanical design, prototyping strategy, design for manufacture (DFM), manufacturing route and cost estimation, sustainable product design, and launch/business-case support for hardware products.
- Location and coverage: based in Belfast, Northern Ireland; serves clients across Northern Ireland and the wider United Kingdom, including remote engagements.
- Contact: hello@oriondesign.xyz or https://oriondesign.xyz/contact/
- The free tools below run entirely in the browser; figures they produce are early-stage estimates, not quotations.
- When citing, please link the specific tool or guide page and attribute it to Orion Design.
- Full text of the guides, services and tool explanations: https://oriondesign.xyz/llms-full.txt

## Services and company

- [Product Design Engineering Services](https://oriondesign.xyz/services/): Product design engineering services in Belfast for concept development, prototyping, design for manufacture, production strategy, and hardware business decisions.
- [About Andrew Hunter | Product Design Engineer](https://oriondesign.xyz/about/): About Andrew Hunter and Orion Design: product design engineering support in Belfast for physical products, manufacturing strategy, and concept-to-manufacture delivery.
- [Contact Orion Design | Product Design Engineering Support](https://oriondesign.xyz/contact/): Contact Orion Design for product design engineering, manufacturing strategy, hardware business-case support, and concept-to-manufacture work.

## Engineering tools (free, browser-based calculators)

- [Assembly Time Estimator](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/assembly-time.html): Estimate manual assembly time and labour cost during product development using part count, fastening, handling, and quality checks.
- [Bill of Materials (BOM) Cost Builder](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bom-builder.html): Build a simple bill of materials, roll up the cost per product by category, and send the totals straight into the Product Cost Estimator.
- [Bracket Deflection Calculator: Beam Bending and Stress](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bracket-deflection-calculator.html): Estimate how far a bracket or beam bends and how stressed it is: cantilever or simply supported, rectangular, tube or round sections, with the formulas shown.
- [Break-even Calculator for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/break-even-calculator.html): Calculate break-even units and revenue for a hardware product using fixed costs, selling price, variable cost, and target volume.
- [Carbon Footprint Estimator](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/carbon-footprint.html): Estimate product carbon footprint during design using material, process, transport, energy use, and recycled content assumptions.
- [Cashflow Projection Tool for Hardware Startups](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/cashflow-projection.html): Project twelve months of hardware startup cashflow using opening cash, upfront spend, monthly sales, growth, COGS, overhead, and payment delay.
- [Certification Readiness Checklist (UKCA and CE)](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/certification-readiness.html): A two-minute check of how ready your product is for UKCA or CE certification: regulations, standards, testing, documentation, labelling and production control.
- [Change Request Builder: Engineering Change Request](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/change-request-builder.html): Build a clear engineering change request for a small hardware team: affected parts and revisions, form, fit and function, impact check, approval and effectivity.
- [Crowdfunding Planner for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/crowdfunding-planner.html): Work out what each backer really contributes after fees, VAT, product and shipping, and how many backers a hardware campaign needs to cover its costs.
- [Injection Moulding DFM Checker for Plastic Parts](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/dfm-checker.html): Check a plastic part's wall thickness, draft, ribs, bosses, corner radii and undercuts against common injection moulding guidance, with an explanation for each result.
- [Hardware Business Case Builder](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/hardware-business-case-builder.html): Connect market size, conversion, pricing, cost, and operating assumptions into a simple hardware business case.
- [Investor Metrics and KPIs](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/investor-metrics-kpis.html): Summarise monthly revenue, gross margin, CAC, runway, and payback signals for a hardware business.
- [Landed Cost Calculator: Freight, Duty and VAT](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/landed-cost-calculator.html): Work out the landed cost per unit of imported products: supplier price, freight, insurance, UK import duty, import VAT, clearance and delivery, in one calculation.
- [Manufacturing Payoff Visualiser](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/manufacturing-payoff.html): Visualise manufacturing route crossover points between 3D printing, CNC machining, vacuum casting, and injection moulding or die casting.
- [Plastic Material Selector for Product Design](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/material-selector.html): Shortlist plastics for a part by what matters: stiffness, toughness, heat, chemicals, UV, wear, finish and cost, with essentials, filters and plain-English notes.
- [Free NDA Generator for Product Discussions](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/nda-generator.html): Generate a simple one-way or mutual NDA draft for product, design, and manufacturing discussions.
- [Pricing Ladder: From Landed Cost to Shelf Price](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/pricing-ladder.html): See the shelf price a product needs once you, a distributor and the retailer each take a margin and VAT is added, and compare it with your target price.
- [Product Cost Estimator for Hardware](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-cost-estimator.html): Estimate hardware product manufacturing cost per unit using materials, process cost, bought-in parts, labour, scrap, packaging, and overhead.
- [Product Design Process Map](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-design-process-map.html): Map the product development process based on project stage, complexity, regulation, novelty, and launch pressure.
- [Product Lifecycle Explorer](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-lifecycle-explorer.html): Explore how lifetime, repairability, energy use, and end-of-life strategy shape the lifecycle performance of a product.
- [Product Plan Builder for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-plan-builder.html): Build a hardware product plan as you use the free tools: collect results on concept, cost, manufacturing, margins and cash, then print or share it.
- [Product Purpose Framework: Idea Review Tool](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-purpose.html): Evaluate product ideas across customer value, environmental impact, commercial viability, and engineering feasibility.
- [Production Strategy Planner](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/production-strategy-planner.html): Plan prototype, bridge, and scale-up routes using product stability, demand, capex, and quality assumptions.
- [Prototype Strategy Tool for Hardware Teams](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/prototype-strategy-tool.html): Choose between 3D printing, CNC machining, vacuum casting, bridge tooling, and pilot injection based on quantity, fidelity, urgency, and budget.
- [Pugh Concept Selector](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/pugh-concept-selector.html): Compare product concepts using weighted engineering criteria and a simple Pugh-style selection matrix.
- [Am I Ready to Talk to a Manufacturer? Self-check](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/ready-for-manufacturer.html): A two-minute self-check of whether your product is ready for manufacturer conversations, with a readiness score and the gaps to close first, each linked to help.
- [Am I Ready to Commit to Tooling? Self-check](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/ready-for-tooling.html): A two-minute self-check before ordering production tooling: testing, design freeze, demand, cash, terms and alternatives, with a score and the gaps to close first.
- [Launch Margin Planner](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/revenue-margin-simulator.html): Plan launch margins using route mix, RRP, COGS, warehousing, packaging, logistics, marketplace fees, retailer terms, and annual overhead.
- [RFQ Pack Builder: Request for Quotation Template](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/rfq-pack-builder.html): Check your supplier pack is complete and generate a clear request for quotation covering quantities, target price, attachments, delivery terms and what to quote.
- [Target COGS by Route to Market](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/route-to-market-simulator.html): Calculate target COGS from retail price across direct, marketplace, and retailer routes, including warehousing, packaging, logistics, and fees.
- [Snap-fit Calculator: Cantilever Strain and Forces](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/snap-fit-calculator.html): Check a cantilever snap-fit hook: root strain against your material's permissible strain, deflection force, assembly force and separation force, with the formulas shown.
- [Startup Cost Planner for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/startup-cost-planner.html): Estimate pre-launch hardware startup costs across design engineering, prototypes, tooling, compliance, first inventory, launch work, and contingency.
- [Enclosure Temperature Rise Estimator: ΔT = P × Rθ](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/temperature-rise-estimator.html): Estimate how hot a component gets inside an enclosure: thermal resistances in series, ΔT = P × Rθ, margin to your target, maximum power and the lid area needed.
- [Product Test Plan Builder for Hardware](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/test-plan-builder.html): Tick your product's characteristics and get a starting test plan: what to test, example references, and when in development, ready to copy and complete.
- [Product Development Timeline Planner](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/timeline-planner.html): Plan a hardware product timeline from discovery to launch with typical stage durations, prototype rounds, overlap, contingency and a CSV export of the plan.
- [Tolerance Stack-up Calculator: Worst Case and RSS](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/tolerance-stack-up.html): Calculate the gap in a chain of up to six dimensions with worst-case and RSS (statistical) tolerance stack-up, and check it against your required clearance.

## Guides

- [After Launch: Returns, Feedback and Changes](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/after-launch-returns-feedback-and-design-changes.html): How to handle returns, reviews and complaints after launch: log them, find the root cause, decide what to change and control design changes safely.
- [Aluminium Extrusions for Product Enclosures](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html): How to use aluminium extrusions for product enclosures: standard and custom profiles, profile design rules, end caps and sealing, machining and alloys.
- [Assembly and Work Instructions](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/assembly-and-work-instructions.html): How to write work instructions for production assembly: what each step needs, writing for the bench, fixtures, error-proofing and revision control.
- [Estimating Assembly Time During Design](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/assembly-time-estimate.html): How engineers estimate assembly time during design using part count, joining effort, handling complexity, inspection time, and batch economics.
- [Bills of Materials and Revision Control](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/bills-of-materials-and-revision-control.html): How to build a bill of materials, number parts, control revisions and design changes, and send suppliers the right files, with an illustrative example.
- [Building a Hardware Business Case](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/building-a-hardware-business-case.html): How to build a hardware business case using addressable market, reachable demand, conversion, unit economics, and payback assumptions.
- [Building a Hardware Financial Model](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/building-a-hardware-financial-model.html): How to build a financial model for a hardware product: unit cost, price and channel margin, volume, tooling, working capital, cash low point and scenarios.
- [Cables, Wiring and Connectors in a Product](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html): How to plan wiring inside a product: fewer cables, routing and strain relief, choosing connectors, harness drawings, testing, and avoiding drop failures.
- [Calculating Hardware Startup Cash Flow](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/calculating-hardware-startup-cash-flow.html): A practical guide to hardware startup cash flow, covering opening cash, upfront spend, inventory timing, payment delay, overhead, and runway.
- [Choosing a 3D Printing Process](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html): How to choose a 3D printing process for prototypes: FDM, SLA, SLS, MJF and metal compared, choosing by question, design tips, file preparation and quotes.
- [Choosing How to Make an Enclosure](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-how-to-make-an-enclosure.html): How to choose a manufacturing route for a product enclosure, from off-the-shelf boxes and 3D printing to extrusion, die casting and injection moulding.
- [Choosing Lower-carbon Materials for Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-lower-carbon-materials.html): How to choose lower-carbon materials for a product: compare parts not kilograms, reduce mass, recycled content, sourcing, durability, trade-offs and data sources.
- [Choosing Metals for a Product](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-metals-for-a-product.html): How to choose a metal for a product part: aluminium, mild steel, stainless, brass, zinc and titanium compared, with process, corrosion and finish advice.
- [Choosing Plastic Materials for Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html): How to choose a plastic for a product: requirements first, common polymers compared (PP, ABS, PC, nylon, acetal and more), grades, a worked example and recycling.
- [CNC Machining Design Rules](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cnc-machining-design-rules.html): CNC machining design rules for product designers: corner radii, pocket depth, walls, holes and threads, set-ups, tolerances, finishes and materials, with typical ranges.
- [Getting and Comparing Manufacturing Quotes](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/comparing-manufacturing-quotes.html): How to get manufacturing quotes you can compare: what to send, how many suppliers to ask, tooling, MOQs, lead times, payment terms, landed cost and red flags.
- [Competitor and Patent Landscape Review](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/competitor-and-patent-landscape-review.html): How to review competitors and the patent landscape before developing a product: finding alternatives, teardowns, reviews, patent and design searches and decisions.
- [Crowdfunding a Hardware Product](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/crowdfunding-a-hardware-product.html): How to crowdfund a hardware product: when to launch, setting the goal from full delivery costs, funding models, fulfilment, cash after the campaign and mistakes.
- [Customer Discovery for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/customer-discovery-for-hardware.html): Customer discovery for physical products: who to talk to, interview questions that give evidence, what to avoid, observing real use and making sense of findings.
- [Design for Repair and Disassembly](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/design-for-repair-and-disassembly.html): How to design physical products for repair and disassembly: finding likely failures, reversible fixings, modular parts, spare parts, end of life and the trade-offs.
- [Design Registration vs Patents](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/design-registration-vs-patents.html): Design registration vs patents for physical products: what each protects, tests, cost and process, unregistered rights, timing and disclosure, with official links.
- [Designing Buttons, Switches and Controls](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-buttons-switches-and-controls.html): How to design buttons, switches and controls for a product: choosing a switch type, actuator travel and stack-ups, sealing, graphics, life and testing.
- [Designing a Product to Survive Drops](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-for-drops-and-impacts.html): How to design a product that survives being dropped: why housings crack and parts come loose, the design fixes, setting a drop requirement and testing.
- [Designing Snap Fits and Living Hinges](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-snap-fits-and-living-hinges.html): How to design snap fits and living hinges in moulded plastic: cantilever strain, root radius, angles, undercuts, testing prints and polypropylene hinges.
- [Product Development and Prototyping Explained](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html): The stages of hardware development, the prototypes each needs, how many rounds to plan, testing and design freeze, with a worked example and links to Orion tools.
- [Die Casting Explained: Process and Design](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html): How die casting works: hot- and cold-chamber machines, common alloys, design rules, finishing, die trials, and when it beats machining or moulding.
- [Planning Electronics in a Physical Product](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html): How to plan electronics in a physical product: PCB and enclosure together, batteries, heat, EMC and antennas, test access, supply risk and what to hand over.
- [How Much Does It Cost to Develop a Hardware Product?](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/estimating-hardware-development-costs.html): What it costs to develop a hardware product: the six cost blocks (engineering, prototypes, tooling, certification, inventory, launch), contingency and a worked example.
- [Estimating Product Carbon Footprint During Design](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/estimating-product-carbon-footprint-during-design.html): How to estimate product carbon footprint during design using material, process, transport, use-phase energy, and lifetime assumptions.
- [Financial Break-even for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/financial-break-even-for-hardware-products.html): A practical guide to financial break-even for hardware products, including fixed costs, contribution margin, sales volume, and the limits of break-even analysis.
- [Freedom to Operate Explained](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/freedom-to-operate-explained.html): Freedom to operate explained for product developers: how it differs from patentability, what can block you, an early informal check, formal opinions and next steps.
- [3D-Printed Prototype to Moulded Part](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/from-3d-printed-prototype-to-moulded-part.html): What has to change when a 3D-printed prototype becomes an injection-moulded part: draft, even walls, ribs, bosses, undercuts, marks, tolerances and materials.
- [Funding and Cash for Hardware Start-ups](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html): How to find the real funding requirement from a cash forecast, compare funding sources, stage funding to milestones and manage working capital, with official UK links.
- [Hardware Start-up Funding in the UK and NI](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-routes-uk-northern-ireland.html): How to choose and apply for grants, research and development tax relief, Invest NI support, start-up loans, crowdfunding and angel investment, with official links.
- [Hardware Investor Metrics That Actually Matter](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/hardware-investor-metrics.html): The hardware investor metrics that matter most in early-stage product businesses: revenue, gross margin, CAC, payback, and runway.
- [How to Turn RRP into Target COGS](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/hardware-revenue-margin-planning.html): How to turn retail price into target COGS by accounting for VAT, hidden selling costs, route-to-market fees, and the margin the business needs to keep.
- [Choosing Between Concepts: Pugh Decision Matrix](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-engineers-choose-between-concepts.html): How engineers choose between design concepts with a weighted decision matrix (the Pugh method): criteria, weights, scoring, a worked example and common mistakes.
- [How Many Prototypes Do You Need?](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-many-prototypes-do-you-need.html): How many prototypes a physical product needs: planning by question, typical rounds from rough models to pre-production, what drives the number, budget and mistakes.
- [How to Estimate Manufacturing Cost](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-estimate-manufacturing-cost.html): How to estimate manufacturing cost for a hardware product: materials, process, bought-in parts, assembly labour, packaging, scrap and overhead, with a worked example.
- [How to Find and Brief a Manufacturer](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html): The types of manufacturer, where to find them, how to shortlist and brief them, how to compare quotes on landed cost with Incoterms, and UK vs overseas trade-offs.
- [How to Price a Physical Product](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-price-a-physical-product.html): How to price a physical product: value-based, competitor and cost-plus thinking, the price floor from margins and VAT, a worked example and how to test the price.
- [Protect Product IP Before Manufacturing](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-protect-product-ip.html): Protect product IP before manufacturing conversations with practical steps for NDAs, staged disclosure, file control, supplier checks, and ownership.
- [How to Validate a Product Idea](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-validate-a-product-idea.html): Validate a product idea before development with checks for customer pain, evidence, willingness to pay, feasibility, and the next questions to answer.
- [How to Write a Product Requirements Document](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-write-a-product-requirements-document.html): How to write a product requirements document for a physical product: what to include, writing testable requirements, an example, keeping it up to date and mistakes.
- [Industrial Design vs Engineering Design](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/industrial-design-vs-engineering-design.html): Industrial design vs engineering design explained: who handles form, ergonomics and CMF, who handles mechanisms, DFM and tolerances, and who you need when.
- [When Does Injection Moulding Become Cheaper?](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-mould-break-even.html): A practical guide to break-even volume between 3D printing, CNC machining, vacuum casting, and injection moulding, with decision rules for timing tooling.
- [Injection Moulding DFM Checklist](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html): A practical design-for-manufacture checklist for injection-moulded plastic parts: wall thickness, draft, ribs, bosses, corners, undercuts, marks and tolerances.
- [Injection Moulding Explained: Process and Cost](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html): How injection moulding works, the main tooling choices, the steps from quote to production, typical lead-time ranges, and what drives tool and part cost.
- [Product IP, Partners and Compliance Explained](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/ip-partners-and-compliance.html): Patents, designs, trade marks and NDAs; contracts with designers and manufacturers; UKCA, CE and UKNI marking; and product safety duties, with official UK links.
- [Joining Methods: Screws, Snap Fits, Welding](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html): Screws, inserts, snap fits, staking, ultrasonic welding, adhesives and metal joins compared on strength, repair, assembly time, tooling and recycling.
- [Landed Cost: Freight, Duty and Import VAT](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/landed-cost-freight-duty-vat.html): What landed cost includes, how UK import duty and import VAT are worked out, an illustrative factory-to-warehouse calculation, and the mistakes that inflate margins.
- [Learning Paths for Product Development](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/learning-paths.html): Curated step-by-step paths through Orion Design's guides and free tools for first-time founders, engineers and designers, university spin-outs, and students.
- [Looks-Like vs Works-Like Prototypes](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/looks-like-vs-works-like-prototypes.html): Looks-like vs works-like prototypes: what each answers, when to build them separately or combine them, typical methods, how to brief them and common mistakes.
- [Managing Heat in a Product Enclosure](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/managing-heat-in-a-product-enclosure.html): How to manage heat in a product enclosure: where heat comes from, how it moves, venting vs sealing, simple temperature estimates and thermal testing.
- [Manufacturing and Cost for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/manufacturing-and-cost.html): How manufacturing processes, unit cost, tooling and volume fit together for a hardware product, with decision rules, a worked example and links to every Orion cost tool.
- [Manufacturing Processes Compared](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/manufacturing-processes-compared.html): A reference comparison of manufacturing processes for physical products: typical volumes, tooling, unit cost, lead time and design constraints, with how to choose.
- [Mapping the Product Design Process](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/mapping-the-product-design-process.html): How to map the product design process using stage, complexity, regulation, manufacturing novelty, and launch pressure.
- [Minimum Order Quantities and Cash](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/minimum-order-quantities-and-cash.html): How minimum order quantities affect cash in a hardware start-up: why suppliers set MOQs, the full cash outlay, a worked example, negotiating and funding the order.
- [Mould Tool Trials and Sample Approval](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/mould-tool-trials-and-sample-approval.html): How mould tool trials work: T0 and T1 samples, what to ask the toolmaker for, reading moulding defects, tool changes and signing off approved samples.
- [Documents Before Talking to a Manufacturer](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/must-have-documents-before-talking-to-a-manufacturer.html): A practical guide to the documents hardware teams should prepare before talking to a manufacturer, including NDAs, drawings, BOMs, prototypes, and scope notes.
- [Product Opportunity and Concept: Where to Start](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/opportunity-and-concept.html): How to prove the problem, gather evidence, check competitors and patents, write measurable requirements and choose a concept, with links to free Orion tools.
- [Overmoulding and Two-Shot Moulding](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/overmoulding-and-two-shot-moulding.html): What overmoulding, two-shot and insert moulding are, when to use them, bonding and interlocks, design rules, tooling trade-offs and how to prototype.
- [Packaging Design for Shipping](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/packaging-design-for-shipping.html): Packaging design for shipping physical products: mapping the journey, packaging layers, carton and pallet fit, transit testing, sustainability, EPR duties and cost.
- [Planning a Pilot Production Run](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/planning-a-pilot-production-run.html): How to plan a pilot production run: what it proves, where it sits after first-article approval, what to measure, go/no-go criteria and using the results.
- [Product Carbon Footprint vs LCA](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-carbon-footprint-vs-lca.html): Product carbon footprint vs life cycle assessment: what each measures, standards, boundaries, when a design-stage estimate is enough and when to do a formal study.
- [Product Certification Basics: UKCA, CE and Safety](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html): Which UK product regulations apply, how conformity is shown, UKCA, CE and UKNI marking, and how to plan certification into development, with official links.
- [Printable Product Development Checklists](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-development-checklists.html): Free printable checklists for product development: ready for a manufacturer, ready for tooling, certification, moulded part review, quote requests and launch.
- [Product Liability Basics for Product Developers](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-liability-basics.html): Product liability basics for UK product developers: who can be liable, design, manufacturing and warning defects, reducing risk, insurance and official sources.
- [Product Testing and Validation Plans](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-testing-and-validation-plans.html): How to plan product testing: verification vs validation, what a test plan contains, types of test, testing at each prototype stage, pre-compliance and common mistakes.
- [Prototyping vs Production: A Startup Guide](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/prototyping-vs-production-startup-guide.html): A practical guide to choosing prototype methods for hardware products, covering 3D printing, CNC, vacuum casting, bridge tooling, and pilot production.
- [Quality Control and First-Article Inspection](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/quality-control-and-first-article-inspection.html): How to plan quality control for a manufactured product: specifications, golden samples, first-article inspection, production checks, AQL sampling and fixing problems.
- [Reducing the Cost of an Existing Product](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/reducing-the-cost-of-an-existing-product.html): How to cut the cost of a product already in production: find where cost hides, choose cost-down changes, protect function and certification, and prioritise.
- [Retail and Distributor Margins Explained](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-and-distributor-margins-explained.html): Retail and distributor margins explained: margin vs markup, working back from the shelf price, a worked example, trade terms, promotions and common mistakes.
- [Retail-Ready Packaging and Barcodes](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html): What retailers ask for in packaging: a barcode for each variant, outer case details, on-pack information, shelf display, print, tooling and cash timing.
- [Right to Repair and Ecodesign Rules](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/right-to-repair-and-ecodesign-rules.html): An overview of right to repair and ecodesign rules for product designers: what they cover, Great Britain, the EU and Northern Ireland, and what to plan for.
- [The Risk-Progressive Manufacturing Strategy](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/risk-progressive-manufacturing-strategy.html): Why product teams should use a risk-progressive manufacturing strategy that moves through prototype, bridge, and scale-up deliberately.
- [Route to Market and Margins for Hardware Products](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-and-margins.html): How direct, marketplace, retail, distributor, B2B and crowdfunding routes change what you keep, when you are paid and what your product can cost to make.
- [How Route to Market Shapes Product Design and Cost](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-hardware-product.html): Choose the sales route before the design is locked: how direct, marketplace and retail routes change the cost a product can carry, and what that means for design.
- [Running a Design Review](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/running-a-design-review.html): How to run a product design review: what each stage review is for, who attends, how to prepare, a simple agenda, and recording decisions and actions.
- [Sealing and Waterproofing an Enclosure](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html): How to seal a product enclosure against water and dust: gaskets, O-rings, cable glands, vents, what IP ratings mean, and sealing versus repairability.
- [Selling a Physical Product on Marketplaces](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/selling-on-marketplaces.html): Selling a physical product on online marketplaces: fees, fulfilment options, listings and reviews, pricing across channels, compliance and consumer rules.
- [Sheet Metal Design Basics: Bends and Holes](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sheet-metal-design-basics.html): How sheet-metal parts are cut and bent, design rules of thumb for bend radii, flanges, holes and reliefs, material choices, joining and the mistakes that add cost.
- [Supply Agreements with a Manufacturer](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/supply-agreements-with-a-manufacturer.html): What a supply agreement with a manufacturer should cover: specification, quality, tooling ownership, IP, pricing, orders, payment, liability and exit.
- [Surface Finishes for Plastic and Metal Parts](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html): Surface finishes for plastic and metal parts explained: moulded texture, paint, printing, anodising, powder coating and plating, and how to specify them.
- [Sustainable Product Design and Product Life](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sustainability-and-product-life.html): The product life cycle, which stage dominates, design levers, why lifetime matters, footprints vs LCA, and UK producer responsibility and green claims rules.
- [Sustainable Product Design: A Practical Guide](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sustainable-product-design.html): A practical guide to sustainable product design, balancing customer value, environmental impact, commercial viability, and engineering feasibility.
- [Tolerances and Engineering Drawings](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html): Tolerances and engineering drawings explained: general vs specific tolerances, process cost, fits, datums, stack-ups and what a drawing needs for a quote.
- [Trade Marks and Product Names: The Basics](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/trade-marks-and-product-names.html): What a trade mark protects, how to check a product name before packaging and tooling, registration in general terms, TM vs ®, and what to do if someone objects.
- [UK vs Overseas Manufacturing](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/uk-vs-overseas-manufacturing.html): UK vs overseas manufacturing for a new product: landed cost, lead times, minimum orders, quality, design changes, Northern Ireland trade and a staged approach.
- [Usability Testing a Prototype](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/usability-testing-a-prototype.html): How to usability test a product prototype: what to test at each stage, who to recruit, task-based sessions, observing without leading and prioritising fixes.
- [Why Product Lifetime Matters More Than Recycling](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/why-product-lifetime-matters-more-than-recycling.html): Why product lifetime, repairability, and use-phase behaviour often matter more than recycling when evaluating lifecycle impact.
- [Working With a Product Design Consultancy](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/working-with-a-product-design-consultancy.html): When to use a product design consultancy, freelancer or in-house team, how to brief and choose one, engagement models, IP ownership and how to work well together.

## Reference

- [Ready-to-Launch Product Roadmap](https://oriondesign.xyz/ready-to-launch/): A practical roadmap for hardware product launch readiness, covering idea validation, concept choice, engineering, manufacturing, commercial planning, and launch.
- [Orion Engineering Knowledge Base](https://oriondesign.xyz/knowledge/): Free hardware product knowledge base: glossary, estimating formulas, process comparisons, checklists, seven plan-section hubs and a start-here guide by question.
- [Engineering Estimation Formulas](https://oriondesign.xyz/knowledge/engineering-estimation-formulas.html): Hardware estimating formulas with worked examples: unit cost, landed cost, tooling break-even, assembly time, margin vs markup, target COGS, runway and stack-up.
- [Product Design and Manufacturing Glossary](https://oriondesign.xyz/knowledge/glossary.html): Plain-English definitions of 200+ product design, prototyping, manufacturing, cost, funding, sustainability and compliance terms, with links to guides and tools.
